topic.title: Self-Supervised Representations and Contrastive Learning
topic.overview: Self-supervised learning constructs training signals from data itself, reducing reliance on manual labels. This cluster focuses on contrastive objectives, informative views, augmentation, and representation quality. A representative framework studies how image transformations, nonlinear projection heads, batch sizes, and training duration affect the usefulness of features learned by contrasting related and unrelated examples.
topic.whyItMatters: The chosen pretext task determines which distinctions a representation preserves or ignores. An invariance helpful for one downstream task may remove information needed by another, so transferability must be evaluated beyond success on the training objective.
topic.evolution: The representatives range from temporal coherence and learning from unlabeled data to modern contrastive visual frameworks. Later papers examine idealized representations, example selection, and generalization theory. Recent applications extend self-supervision to textures and tabular data, adapting the encoding to domain-specific structure.
openQuestions: How can augmentations be chosen when future tasks are unknown?
Which representation-quality measures predict transfer across domains rather than performance on a familiar benchmark?

papers.tldr: SelfClean uses self-supervised representations and distance-based indicators to find image dataset issues and improve evaluation reliability.

papers.title: Learning from Teaching Regularization: Generalizable Correlations Should be Easy to Imitate
papers.tldr: LoT uses feedback from auxiliary students to encourage a main model to learn relationships that are easier to imitate and generalize.

papers.title: Learning predictable and robust neural representations by straightening image sequences
papers.tldr: Encouraging straight trajectories through representation space produces predictive, factorized, and more robust visual embeddings in the studied setting.

papers.title: Localizing Memorization in SSL Vision Encoders
papers.tldr: LayerMem and UnitMem locate memorization inside self-supervised vision encoders, revealing patterns relevant to fine-tuning and pruning.

papers.title: No Train, all Gain: Self-Supervised Gradients Improve Deep Frozen Representations
papers.tldr: FUNGI augments frozen model embeddings with compressed self-supervised gradients, improving representations without additional training.

papers.title: Preventing Dimensional Collapse in Self-Supervised Learning via Orthogonality Regularization
papers.tldr: Orthogonality regularization throughout the encoder mitigates dimensional collapse and consistently improves evaluated self-supervised CNN and Transformer models.

papers.title: Self-Guided Masked Autoencoder
papers.tldr: Self-guided masked autoencoding uses emerging patch clusters to choose informed masks and improve learning without external supervision.

papers.title: Self-supervised Transformation Learning for Equivariant Representations
papers.tldr: STL learns transformation representations from image pairs, enabling equivariant learning with complex augmentations and improving several classification and detection benchmarks.

papers.title: Understanding the Role of Equivariance in Self-supervised Learning
papers.tldr: An information-theoretic analysis explains how predicting transformations can encourage semantic features that help downstream tasks.

papers.title: You Don’t Need Domain-Specific Data Augmentations When Scaling Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: A DINOv2 case study achieves strong representations with cropping alone when training data is sufficiently large.

papers.title: An Augmentation-Aware Theory for Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning
papers.tldr: An augmentation-aware error bound connects contrastive learning performance to an explicit trade-off introduced by data augmentation.

papers.title: Clustering Properties of Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: ReSA uses the encoder’s strong clustering structure to guide self-supervised learning, improving benchmark performance and clustering at multiple levels.

papers.title: Collapse-Proof Non-Contrastive Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: A projector and loss based on hyperdimensional computing encourage clustered, decorrelated representations and provably avoid several forms of collapse.

papers.title: Discovering Global False Negatives On the Fly for Self-supervised Contrastive Learning
papers.tldr: GloFND learns anchor-specific thresholds during training to detect false negatives across a dataset with dataset-size-independent per-iteration cost.

papers.title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
papers.tldr: Matryoshka sparse autoencoders preserve broad and specific concepts through nested dictionaries, improving interpretability tasks with a small reconstruction tradeoff.

papers.title: NeuronTune: Towards Self-Guided Spurious Bias Mitigation
papers.tldr: NeuronTune probes and regulates internal neurons to reduce spurious prediction behavior without annotations of the spurious correlations.

papers.title: On the Importance of Embedding Norms in Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: Embedding norms affect self-supervised learning speed and encode confidence even when models compare embeddings using cosine similarity.

papers.title: scSSL-Bench: Benchmarking Self-Supervised Learning for Single-Cell Data
papers.tldr: scSSL-Bench compares nineteen methods and finds task-specific winners, with random masking the strongest augmentation across its evaluated single-cell tasks.

papers.title: Self-Organizing Visual Prototypes for Non-Parametric Representation Learning
papers.tldr: SOP learns visual features using multiple complementary support embeddings per prototype, improving results on many retrieval benchmarks.

papers.title: A Statistical Theory of Contrastive Learning via Approximate Sufficient Statistics
papers.tldr: A statistical framework connects contrastive learning to approximate information preservation and explains how that supports downstream prediction.

papers.title: Adv-SSL: Adversarial Self-Supervised Representation Learning with Theoretical Guarantees
papers.tldr: Adv-SSL uses adversarial optimization to address biased self-supervised objectives and supports effective transfer with few labels.

papers.title: BMW: Bidirectionally Memory bank reWriting for Unsupervised Person Re-Identification
papers.tldr: BMW improves unsupervised person re-identification by updating memory banks to make each class more compact and different classes more distinct.

papers.title: Confusion-Driven Self-Supervised Progressively Weighted Ensemble Learning for Non-Exemplar Class Incremental Learning
papers.tldr: CLOVER combines confusion-focused representation learning with a progressively weighted ensemble to learn new classes without retaining old examples.

papers.title: CoUn: Empowering Machine Unlearning via Contrastive Learning
papers.tldr: CoUn uses contrastive and supervised learning on retained data to improve removal of forgotten data's influence.

papers.title: Ditch the Denoiser: Emergence of Noise Robustness in Self-Supervised Learning from Data Curriculum
papers.tldr: A denoised-to-noisy training curriculum helps self-supervised models internalize noise robustness so the denoiser can be discarded after pretraining.

papers.title: Enhancing Contrastive Learning with Variable Similarity
papers.tldr: CLVS improves contrastive learning by assigning lower target similarity to more strongly augmented views.

papers.title: Exploring Structural Degradation in Dense Representations for Self-supervised Learning
papers.tldr: Self-supervised representations can deteriorate for dense tasks during longer training, and a structural estimator helps select checkpoints and reduce degradation.

papers.title: Joint‑Embedding vs Reconstruction: Provable Benefits of Latent Space Prediction for Self‑Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: The analysis shows that joint embedding needs weaker augmentation alignment than reconstruction when irrelevant features have large magnitude.

papers.title: Learning Without Augmenting: Unsupervised Time Series Representation Learning via Frame Projections
papers.tldr: The method learns time-series representations from complementary frame projections, reporting gains without strong handcrafted augmentations.

papers.title: Minimal Semantic Sufficiency Meets Unsupervised Domain Generalization
papers.tldr: MS-UDG learns representations that preserve shared semantics and remove irrelevant variation, improving domain generalization without category or domain labels.

papers.title: Mitigating Spurious Features in Contrastive Learning with Spectral Regularization
papers.tldr: Encouraging a more uniform feature spectrum improves robustness and transfer in tested self-supervised models without requiring labels.

papers.title: Multi-modal contrastive learning adapts to intrinsic dimensions of shared latent variables
papers.tldr: With temperature optimization, multimodal contrastive learning can preserve shared information while adapting to its lower intrinsic dimensionality.

papers.title: Revitalizing SVD for Global Covariance Pooling: Halley’s Method to Overcome Over-Flattening
papers.tldr: Halley-SVD improves covariance pooling by combining stable early gradients with preservation of large eigenvalues later in training.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Contrastive Learning is Approximately Supervised Contrastive Learning
papers.tldr: The paper shows how self-supervised contrastive learning approximates a supervised objective and links its representation geometry to few-shot classification.

papers.title: Self-supervised Learning of Echocardiographic Video Representations via Online Cluster Distillation
papers.tldr: DISCOVR transfers anatomical information from an evolving image encoder into a video encoder to improve self-supervised heart-ultrasound representations.

papers.title: seq-JEPA: Autoregressive Predictive Learning of Invariant-Equivariant World Models
papers.tldr: Seq-JEPA predicts representations across view-and-action sequences to learn separate invariant and equivariant features with strong results on both task types.

papers.title: T-REGS: Minimum Spanning Tree Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: T-REGS uses minimum-spanning-tree length to mitigate representation collapse and encourage uniformity, with theoretical analysis and experimental support.

papers.title: A Random Matrix Theory of Masked Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: A high-dimensional analysis identifies when masked self-supervised learning recovers latent signals and structured settings where it provably outperforms PCA.

papers.title: CURE: Consistency-under-Unified Semantic Regularization for Generalized Category Discovery
papers.tldr: CURE separates representation learning into stages to preserve semantic structure and improve discovery of previously unseen categories.

papers.title: Directional Neural Collapse Explains Few-Shot Transfer in Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: Low representation variability along class-separating directions helps explain few-shot transfer and, under stated labeling assumptions, reduced interference across tasks.

papers.title: Divide and Contrast: Learning Robust Temporal Features without Augmentation
papers.tldr: Di-COT learns transferable time-series features by contrasting overlapping sub-blocks, reducing training cost without data augmentation.

papers.title: FairSSL: Fair Multimodal Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: FairSSL learns from heterogeneous multimodal data using subject-aware regularization, improving reported fairness without reducing predictive performance.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Contrastive Learning for Few-Shot Automatic Modulation Recognition
papers.tldr: DyCo-CL combines geometry-aware augmentation, semantic consistency, and physical priors to improve modulation recognition with very few labeled examples.

papers.title: IdEst: Assessing Self-Supervised Learning Representations via Intrinsic Dimension
papers.tldr: IdEst uses intrinsic dimension to assess self-supervised representations and select hyperparameters at lower cost than supervised probing.

papers.title: Interpretable Self-Supervised Learning via Representer Landmarks and Nyström Approximation
papers.tldr: KREPES explains self-supervised representations through influential unlabeled examples and scales analytical auditing to million-sample datasets.

papers.title: Multiview Self-Representation Learning across Heterogeneous Views
papers.tldr: MSRL learns invariant visual representations from heterogeneous pretrained features through self-representation and cross-view assignment consistency.

papers.title: Newton-coupled Dual-Teacher Semi-supervised Learning Framework
papers.tldr: TTN combines two teachers’ predictions and loss curvature to guide more effective semi-supervised student learning.

papers.title: Position: Unlabeled $\not =$ No Human Supervision in Visual Learning
papers.tldr: Visual-learning papers should disclose human assumptions in data curation and objectives, even when training data has no labels.

papers.title: SAEmnesia: Erasing Concepts in Diffusion Models with Supervised Sparse Autoencoders
papers.tldr: SAEmnesia concentrates concepts into individual sparse-autoencoder neurons to make diffusion-model concept erasure more targeted and efficient.

papers.title: Self-Supervised Learning as Discrete Communication
papers.tldr: Training a student to predict a teacher's capacity-limited binary messages produces structured visual representations with reported gains across several tasks.

papers.title: Statistical Consistency and Generalization of Contrastive Representation Learning
papers.tldr: The paper links contrastive loss to optimal retrieval ranking and derives generalization bounds that improve with larger negative sets.

papers.title: STD-Former: Image-Conditioned Texture Dictionary Encoding with Sparse Topological Supervision for Texture Recognition
papers.tldr: STD-Former builds a texture dictionary from each input image and optionally adds sparse topological supervision to improve recognition.

papers.title: TabularBERT: Binning-Based Self-Supervised Learning for Tabular Representation
papers.tldr: TabularBERT combines numerical binning with masked Transformer pretraining to learn tabular representations that account for proximity, order, and cross-variable dependencies.
